title.narrative: Indicator 4.2 of participants feeling more equipped with new knowledge and skills related to gender, protection, respectful confrontation and gender transformative approach.

description.narrative: this indicator measures the of participants in the trainings reporting feeling more equipped with new knowledge and skills related to gender, protection, respectful confrontation and gender transformative approach as a result of the training and in comparison with their feeling at the start of the project

comment.narrative: SoVs activity reports prepost survey participants feedbackThe indicator counts the number of staff and CPCs member that have participated in both training programs and after assessment feel more equipped with new knowledge and skills related to gender protection respectful confrontation and gender transformative approach. The target will be considered achieved when the two training programs have been delivered and the data of participants improvement have been analyzed. So far a 5days training program and 20 coaching sessions have been carried out counting with 104 participants.The target for participants in the training and coaching sessions was reduced from 120 individuals to 100 individuals. During implementation it was realized that the number of staff involved in the project for whom the training would be relevant was lower than the target originally set during the proposal drafting stage. Therefore the target was adjusted to reflect the actual number of individuals who would benefit from the training and coaching sessions

title.narrative: Indicator 1.2: of agricultural water wells rehabilitated

description.narrative: this indicator measures the number of agricultural wells rehabilitated under output 1

comment.narrative: SoV Construction reportstraining reportsphotosMoUs BoQsThis indicator counts the number of agricultural wells rehabilitated once the handover certificate is signed and the construction report from the supplier received. During the reporting period two water wells were carefully selected based on established standard operating procedures and verified through crosschecking with relevant ministries and sectors. One of the wells has been fully rehabilitated and equipped with a solar panel resulting in reduced water pumping costs that benefit the 42 farmers who use this well. The bidding process for the rehabilitation of the second well has been put on hold due to cost savings achieved in other activities. The saved funds were reallocated to the rehabilitation of an additional well. To ensure efficiency both projects will be consolidated under a single bidding process. The bidding process will be launched and the rehabilitation work carried out in the coming months.
